newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House bans funds for suicide help.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House bans funds for suicide help.

text.p: The U.S. House of Representatives easily voted Wednesday to ban federal funds for physician-assisted suicide.

The measure, approved with only a handful of Democratic dissenters, is largely symbolic at this point because no state allows assisted suicide. But a Supreme Court ruling expected in July could pave the way for states to legalize doctor-assisted deaths.
The bill does not bar a patient from refusing medical treatment, food or water near the end of life, nor does it block access to powerful painkillers.

The Senate has not begun work on a companion bill, but House sponsors expect it to do so soon. President Bill Clinton has voiced his opposition to assisted suicide, and the White House signaled that he would sign this bill.

The bill would bar Medicare, the federal portion of Medicaid, or other public health and veteran's health services from paying for physician-assisted suicide. States could use their own Medicaid and health funds if the Supreme Court gives the go-ahead.
It also sets up some pilot programs to improve medical treatment of pain and depression, although it does not go as far as some Democrats had hoped.
